subject: Re: Furnova – third-party roster, KMS flow & quick QA

Subject: Furnova – request: vendor roster + KMS flow

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Furnova’s Security & Procurement teams asked for a short packet we can use for our vendor risk review: specifically
- a current roster of all subprocessors that process Furnova customer data (names, primary function, country of processing),
- a simple KMS/keyholder diagram showing where customer data keys are stored and how ephemeral worker nodes request keys, and
- a recent SOC 2 snapshot or an attestation page we can share with our auditors.

Can you surface what’s available today? If possible, we’d like anything that confirms: no subprocessor in Russia/Belarus, at-rest encryption with customer-data-specific CMKs, and a sample of audit log output for deletion/DSAR actions.

We’re on a tight review window — ideally by EOD Friday (05/14). Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Information Security Manager
Furnova, Inc.

--
Lena O.
Furnova Security
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. I’m attaching a concise packet: subprocessor roster (CSV), a one-page KMS flow diagram, a SOC 2 snapshot (redacted PII sections) and a short sample of audit log lines showing delete operations.

Quick notes while you review:
- The roster includes all third parties that handle Furnova customer content for production inference and storage. We’ve tagged each vendor with processing region and primary purpose column.
- No subprocessors in Russia/Belarus; EU processing is handled by our EU cluster partners listed in the roster.
- We use customer-segregated CMKs in KMS for Hosted Dedicated customers who require key isolation; the diagram shows the key rotation and ephemeral worker decrypt flow.
- The audit sample is a short text file with anonymized event ids and timestamps (no customer content).

If you need additional proof (e.g., a KMS key policy snippet, or a runbook excerpt for DSAR handling), say the word and we’ll add it. We can also redline a minimal attestation if your auditors need a specific line.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v2.csv (CSV), kms_key_flow.png (PNG), soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf (PDF), audit_log_sample.txt (TXT)

Thanks — Kim

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@furnova.com>

Kim,

Received the attachments — very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from our side after an initial pass:
1) For the subprocessor roster: can you add a column that indicates whether the vendor has access to decrypted customer content (yes/no)? Right now purpose alone is not enough for our classification.
2) For KMS: can you confirm whether key material ever leaves the cloud provider’s KMS (i.e., are there any external HSM transfers or on-prem signing involved)? A simple yes/no and one-sentence explanation will do.
3) For the audit logs: are those logs stored in a write-once location or can they be modified by admins? We need an assurance that audit logs are immutable for at least 90 days.

If you can return these three points by EOD Friday, we can move to the contract ops review on Monday.

Also — small ask: is there a pre-signed DocuSign link for the addendum we discussed (data processing terms)? We have procurement lined up but want an executed addendum before the SOW starts.

Best,
Lena
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@furnova.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-14T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Furnova – request: vendor roster + KMS flow

Lena — quick follow-up with the three answers below and two action items. Apologies for the rapid-fire — wanted to keep within your review window.

1) Decrypted access flag: updated column added to roster. Short summary: only our storage provider and the inference runtime (short-lived workers) have the ability to decrypt plaintext for active serving; we’ve set the roster flag to "Yes" for those two categories and "No" for analytics/monitoring vendors.

2) KMS export: No — key material does not leave the cloud provider KMS. We do not perform external HSM transfers. Customer CMKs are managed in the cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS depending on region). Key wrapping/unwrapping happens in-hosted workers that request ephemeral data keys; the master key never leaves KMS.

3) Audit log immutability: Audit logs are written to an append-only bucket with object versioning + retention policy (90 days min for Hosted customers). Only a restricted SRE group can initiate retention extension; audit records themselves are immutable for the retention window.

Action items:
- Rishi: please attach the updated CSV with the decrypted-access column and push to the secure Share link (redwood-secure-drive/furnova/).
- Karthik: can you drop a one-sentence KMS key policy excerpt that says CMKs are non-exportable? I’ll include that in the attestation bundle.

We’ll also include a DocuSign link for the addendum; expect that from Sales Ops (Rishi) within 24 hours.

If anything else is required for the audit, we can schedule a 30-minute screen share with your security engineers.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts (Security Liaison)
Redwood Inference

- audit_log_sample.txt (anonymized event ids; timestamps; event types: DELETE, DSAR_REQUEST, KEY_ROTATE)
